1.explanation: The F# language definition lives in components/prism-fsharp.js (and its minified counterpart). This file’s grammar currently does not include a rule to match type annotations (the colon plus the type identifier). To highlight annotations correctly, you must extend or adjust the token patterns in these files so that Prism recognizes " : TypeName" as a separate token (e.g. a `type` or `symbol` token). Without updating these files, Prism will continue to treat type annotations as plain text.
1.bug_scenario: When Prism renders F# code, the type annotations following a colon (for example, the “: MyRecord” or “: double” in function parameters or let-bindings) are not being tokenized and highlighted. In the screenshots, you can see that keywords, union cases and record fields are colored, but the type names and the colon remain in the default text color, whereas in Visual Studio those annotations all receive the “type” styling.

2.explanation: All of Prism’s language support is driven by the definitions in the components folder. The F# grammar in prism-fsharp.js is responsible for tokenizing union cases, record fields and annotations. Currently it doesn’t include a pattern to recognize the colon-prefixed type names, so they’re left un-tokenized (and thus un-colored). The minified version prism-fsharp.min.js is the production build of the same grammar, so both files will need to be updated to add the proper regex or lookbehind to capture type annotations and assign them the “type” token class.
2.bug_scenario: When Prism renders F# code it correctly highlights keywords like “type” and union cases, but it fails to highlight the type names in annotations (the “: MyRecord”, “: int”, “: double” parts). In the screenshot you can see that Prism treats the colon and the type identifier after it as plain text, whereas in the Visual Studio example these types receive their own color class.
